about: How a person is named wherever they appear: as a sender, in a mention, in a notification, a list or a header. Their display name in the room comes first, then the name on their own profile, then the localpart of their ID (between the @ and the colon), only when nothing else is known. A name is trimmed; an empty name, or one that is the person's own ID, counts as none. A name the SDK marks ambiguous (another member of the room has it) is followed by the ID in parentheses, as Element shows it, and so is a name that looks like an ID (an @ later followed by a colon or a dot) or hides characters (U+2000 to U+200D, U+0300 to U+036F, U+2062, U+2063, U+2800, U+061C, U+FEFF). A mention reads @ and the name. memberName and globalName are null when unknown, as before the member list or profile arrives.

cases.case: The room's name before their profile's
cases.name: Sam (design)

cases.case: Their profile's name when the room has none
cases.name: Sam Okafor

cases.case: The localpart only when nothing else is known
cases.name: sam

cases.case: An empty name counts as none
cases.name: Sam Okafor

cases.case: A blank name counts as none
cases.name: sam

cases.case: Their own ID as a name counts as none
cases.name: sam

cases.case: A name another member shares gets the ID
cases.name: Sam (@sam:example.org)

cases.case: A name that looks like someone else's ID gets the ID
cases.name: @sam:example.org (@mallory:example.org)

cases.case: A profile name that looks like an ID gets the ID
cases.name: @bob.example.org (@eve:example.org)

cases.case: A name hiding characters gets the ID
cases.name: Sam​Okafor (@sam2:example.org)

cases.case: An ID on a server with a port
cases.name: ops

textAbout: A user ID written in plain text, as in a notification or an Activity line, reads as a mention of that person: @ and their name from the room's members, already worked out by the rules above, or @ and the localpart when the room doesn't know them. @room stays as it is, and so does an ID inside a word.

text.case: A member's ID reads as their name
An unknown ID reads as its localpart
An ID inside a word stays
Text without an ID is unchanged

pillsAbout: A mention in a message, as a pill or as an ID typed in its text, reads as @ and the name the room knows that person by now, whatever label the sender's app gave it. Someone the room doesn't know keeps the pill's label, or @ and the localpart. A pill is one mention even when an older app split it in two links. Each case gives the message's body, its HTML or null, and the room's members; the result is the message's text as shown.

pills.case: A pill labelled with the ID reads as the name
A pill with an old label reads as the current name
A pill for someone the room doesn't know keeps its label
An ID typed as text reads as the name
An unknown ID typed as text reads as its localpart
A pill split in two links is one name
